To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in deeply supercooled liquids the distribution of the self-diffusivities acquires, for some timescales, a bimodal shape that is associated with the coexistence of a high- and a low- diffusivity phase.
in the supercooled regime, the distribution of the particle diffusivities is bimodal.
the single-particle diffusion coefficient distribution acquires a bimodal shape, and that the coexistence timescale of the two phases grows faster than the structural relaxation time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the dynamical properties of glassy materials, and in particular of supercooled liquid systems.
the dynamics of super-cooled liquids and glasses.
the study of the dynamical heterogeneity of glass-forming systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics of supercooling liquids is heterogeneous and that the dynamics of a single particle is characterized by a distribution of diffusivities.
the dynamics of glass-forming liquids is characterized by the coexistence of at least two phases with different relaxation times.

the glassy state is a dynamical phase, characterized by a nontrivial dynamical heterogeneity, and that this dynamical heterogeneity is the origin of the breakdown of the thermodynamic and the Stokes-Einstein relations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of super-cooled liquids is heterogeneous, with two phases coexisting on timescales growing faster than the structural relaxation time on cooling.
we provide the first experimental evidence that in deeply supercooled liquids two different diffusivities can coexist for timescales growing with the cooling rate.
we have shown that the distribution of the diffusivity of a single particle in a glass-forming liquid is not a simple function of the time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in deeply supercooled liquids, a bimodality in the distribution of the diffusivities is the fingerprint of dynamical coexistence.
the dynamics of super-cooled liquids is heterogeneous, and this heterogeneity is reflected in the transient bimodality of the diffusivity distribution.

, although the non-ergodicity parameter is not able to capture the coexistence of different dynamical phases, it is possible to measure directly the distribution of diffusivities and the coexistence of phases with different diffusive behavior, and that this coexistence is a key feature of supercooled and glassy systems.
